subject: CloudPort sprint-zero: ramp playbook & listing exceptions
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cloudport.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: CloudPort Integrations <partners@cloudport.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint-0 & marketplace constraints (CloudPort x Redwood)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for taking the time at the partner summit. CloudPort is ready to kick off a sprint-zero to validate the integration pattern for our ISV channel (Acme Retail is the pilot). Before we lock calendar slots, wanted to capture a few constraints so we can build a compact ramp playbook: 

- Marketplace listing constraints: CloudPort requires a billing SKU per deployment model (hosted / dedicated / private); listing must include a trial entitlement mapping. Are SKU-level metering hooks supported today?
- Entitlements: Acme requires data-retention controls and a per-tenant export of request logs (for their auditors). Do you have an existing export endpoint or will we need a one-off job?
- Binary artifacts and compatibility: our SI has a hardened runtime that only accepts quantized weights under a specific format; will Redwood Verify be able to sign/verify quantized artifacts?
- Legal & procurement: Acme's procurement team asked for a two-week review window and a single subscription SKU for their POC. Any playbook on exceptions?

I've attached a short requirements brief (cloudport_sprint0_requirements.pdf). Can we schedule a 45-minute kickoff next week to walk tech + legal?

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Integrations, CloudPort Solutions
attachments: cloudport_sprint0_requirements.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cloudport.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint-0 & marketplace constraints (CloudPort x Redwood)

Sanjay — appreciate the clear brief. Looping in KarThik (platform/integration) and Ben (partner ops) to scope the sprint-zero. High level proposed playbook:

1) Discovery call (45m) — infra and compliance asks (this week)
2) Sandbox runbook — we provision a CloudPort tenant on Redwood Hosted + a Dedicated mirror for performance tests
3) Entitlement mapping — KarThik will list required APIs/exports and flag any gaps for Acme's auditors
4) Listing checklist & SKU map — Ben will propose temporary POC SKU and billing flow for marketplace listing exception
5) Acceptance criteria — shared regression prompts and perf targets for 95th perc token latency (< 200ms for hosted)

Internal asks for sprint-zero:
- KarThik: can you confirm whether we can deliver a tenant-level request-log export (S3 presigned + retention policy) within 2 weeks?
- Ben: what is the shortest procurement path to agree a single POC SKU and temporary waiver for the marketplace catalog?
- Legal: will need to sign off on a limited-term exception for the trial SKU and a reduced data-retention SLA.

I attached MA questions we typically share in sprint-zero (ma_questions_v1.xlsx). Proposed kickoff slots: Wed 7/5 10:30-11:15 or Thu 7/6 13:00-13:45 PT. Which works for you?

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Partner GTM, Redwood Inference
attachments: ma_questions_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cloudport.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint-0 & marketplace constraints (CloudPort x Redwood)

Thanks Irene / Sanjay — quick technical clarifications from platform:

- Tenant-level log export: yes, we can deliver an S3 export pipeline that produces daily manifests. Two-week delivery is tight but feasible if we scope to a rolling-export (no ad-hoc queries). Deliverable: presigned S3 path + retention policy config. Jira: INTEGR-402.
- Quantized artifacts: our Verify tool supports int8/4-bit quant formats commonly used by SIs, but CloudPort's hardened runtime requires a signed manifest and a checksum in a custom header. We can add a signing step (small dev effort) — Jira: INTEGR-408. Need CloudPort to share the expected checksum header format.
- Billing hooks / SKU metering: hosted metering is available via token metering today. Dedicated / Private require a usage bridge; we can surface a CSV/billing export.
- Security questionnaire: some control gaps for on-prem private connector (we don't have an air-gapped installer image with HSM integration stamped for FedRAMP) — will need a scoped exception and a timeline.

Requested next steps:
- Sanjay: share checksum header sample and Acme's auditor export format (example CSV)
- Irene: confirm kickoff time and which Redwood engineers should join the call (I can bring runtime + infra).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cloudport.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint-0 & marketplace constraints (CloudPort x Redwood)

Folks — commercial-side notes and an ask for Ops: 

- Temporary POC SKU: we can issue a single subscription SKU scoped to Acme's POC for 60 days. We'll need a short addendum signed by Acme (legal).
- Marketplace exception: to list without the standard entitlement mapping, we need a Product Ops waiver. I can route that but will need: (a) a clear trial SKU description, (b) expected monthly seats/volume, (c) start/end dates for the waiver.
- Procurement: Acme's procurement (Lena Ortiz) prefers a single purchase order and Net-30 standard terms; attach billing_sku_map.csv for mapping.

DocuSign: I've created a placeholder MSA addendum for the POC: https://docusign.com/transactions/ABC-12345
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/DEAL-9723
Jira tickets opened for delivery: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INTEGR-402, https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INTEGR-408

Ben Carter
Partner Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: billing_sku_map.csv (csv, 8KB)

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@cloudport.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmeretail.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2028 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint-0 & marketplace constraints (CloudPort x Redwood)

Great — thanks everyone. Wed 7/5 and Thu 7/6 are both fine for a kickoff; let's take Thu 7/6 13:00 PT to give our legal a chance to scan the MSA addendum beforehand.

Action items we will take before kickoff:
- Share checksum header spec and sample signed manifest (Sanjay) — will attach to the Jira ticket INTEGR-408.
- Provide Acme's auditor CSV template for logs (Lena) — she'll upload to the Drive folder.
- Procurement: Lena will prepare a single PO and sign the DocuSign once Redwood confirms the POC SKU mapping.

I'll upload the samples to the shared Drive and drop the link in Jira. Looking forward to the kickoff.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Integrations, CloudPort Solutions
